workflow_sequence.description: Application startup: Program.cs reads connection string from appsettings.json
Backend registers ApplicationDbContext with Entity Framework Core using SQL Server provider
Backend registers SQL-backed repositories (SqlTransactionRepository, SqlAccountRepository) in dependency injection
Application startup: Seed data initialization creates test accounts in SQL database
API request arrives: Controller calls service layer to validate and process transaction
Service validates transaction rules and calls SQL repository to persist transaction
SQL repository executes INSERT via Entity Framework Core and returns persisted transaction
API response returns transaction to client with HTTP 201 Created

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Read connection string from appsettings.json and validate it exists
new_responsibilities.intent: Configuration is available at startup; backend must ensure database connectivity before accepting requests

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Register ApplicationDbContext with Entity Framework Core using SQL Server provider
new_responsibilities.intent: Backend owns dependency injection and service registration; DbContext must be configured before repositories are instantiated

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Register SQL-backed repositories instead of in-memory repositories
new_responsibilities.intent: Backend controls which repository implementation is used; this is a dependency injection concern

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Initialize seed data using SQL repositories on startup
new_responsibilities.intent: Backend owns application initialization logic; seed data must be created in SQL database, not in-memory

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Handle database connection failures gracefully with meaningful error messages
new_responsibilities.intent: Backend is the defensible zone for error handling; users should receive clear feedback about database issues

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Define DbSet<Account> and DbSet<Transaction> in ApplicationDbContext
new_responsibilities.intent: Entity Framework Core requires DbSet properties to map domain models to database tables

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Configure entity mappings in OnModelCreating using Fluent API
new_responsibilities.intent: Database schema design (column names, types, constraints) must be defined in code to match app/src/db/schema.sql

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Implement SqlTransactionRepository with LINQ queries against DbContext
new_responsibilities.intent: Repository is the data access layer; it must translate ITransactionRepository interface calls to Entity Framework Core queries

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Implement SqlAccountRepository with LINQ queries and balance calculation
new_responsibilities.intent: Repository must implement IAccountRepository interface; balance calculation queries transactions from SQL database

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Ensure transaction atomicity for financial operations
new_responsibilities.intent: Database layer must guarantee data integrity; financial transactions must be all-or-nothing
Configuration layer manages environment differences; different databases for dev/test/prod

architectural_decisions.decision: Use Entity Framework Core with SQL Server provider for SQL database access
architectural_decisions.justification: Entity Framework Core is already referenced in the project and provides LINQ-based data access that maintains the repository pattern. SQL Server is configured in appsettings.json.
architectural_decisions.basis: Existing project setup and appsettings.json configuration
architectural_decisions.impact: Requires Entity Framework Core NuGet package and SQL Server provider; all data access goes through DbContext
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: What is the target SQL database platform?

architectural_decisions.decision: Implement SQL repositories (SqlTransactionRepository, SqlAccountRepository) that implement existing interfaces
architectural_decisions.justification: Maintains the repository pattern and interface contracts; allows controllers and services to remain unchanged. This is a drop-in replacement for in-memory repositories.
architectural_decisions.basis: Existing repository interface pattern in codebase
architectural_decisions.impact: New repository implementations required; no changes to controllers, services, or API contracts
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Should existing API endpoints continue to work with SQL-backed repositories?

architectural_decisions.decision: Configure ApplicationDbContext with Fluent API mappings in OnModelCreating
architectural_decisions.justification: Fluent API provides explicit control over entity mappings, constraints, and indexes. This ensures the C# domain models map correctly to the SQL schema defined in app/src/db/schema.sql.
architectural_decisions.basis: Entity Framework Core best practice; matches existing ApplicationDbContext structure
architectural_decisions.impact: ApplicationDbContext must be updated with DbSet properties and OnModelCreating configuration
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: What is the complete database schema design for Account and Transaction entities?

architectural_decisions.decision: Use automatic database migrations via Entity Framework Core on application startup
architectural_decisions.justification: Simplifies deployment and ensures schema is always in sync with code. EF Core can generate migrations from entity mappings.
architectural_decisions.basis: Common pattern in .NET applications; reduces manual deployment steps
architectural_decisions.impact: Requires EF Core migration infrastructure; database must be accessible at startup
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Should database migrations be automated or manual?

architectural_decisions.decision: Update seed data initialization to use SQL repositories instead of in-memory
architectural_decisions.justification: Seed data must be persisted to SQL database for consistency. Current Program.cs logic can be adapted to use SQL repositories.
architectural_decisions.basis: Requirement from story analysis; ensures test data is available after application restart
architectural_decisions.impact: Program.cs startup logic must be updated; seed data initialization must check for existing data to avoid duplicates
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Should existing in-memory seed data be migrated to SQL database?

architectural_decisions.decision: Maintain connection string in appsettings.json with environment-specific overrides
architectural_decisions.justification: Configuration-driven connection strings allow different databases per environment (dev/test/prod). appsettings.Development.json can override for local development.
architectural_decisions.basis: Existing appsettings.json structure; .NET configuration best practice
architectural_decisions.impact: Connection string must be valid and database must be accessible; application startup fails if connection fails
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: What is the target SQL database platform?

architectural_decisions.decision: Add error handling for database connection failures in Program.cs
architectural_decisions.justification: Provides meaningful error messages when database is unavailable. Prevents cryptic Entity Framework Core exceptions from reaching users.
architectural_decisions.basis: Story analysis requirement for error handling
architectural_decisions.impact: Application startup may fail with clear error message if database is unavailable
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Error handling for database connection failures

architectural_decisions.decision: Resolve database platform mismatch: Use SQL Server (not PostgreSQL) for .NET API
architectural_decisions.justification: appsettings.json specifies SQL Server connection string. The PostgreSQL schema in app/src/db is for reference/testing only. SQL Server schema will be created via Entity Framework Core migrations.
architectural_decisions.basis: Explicit Architectural Change from Story - appsettings.json is the source of truth for production database
architectural_decisions.impact: Entity Framework Core mappings must target SQL Server syntax; UUID types become UNIQUEIDENTIFIER in SQL Server
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: What is the target SQL database platform?

questions_addressed.question: What is the target SQL database platform?
questions_addressed.answer: SQL Server (as specified in appsettings.json connection string)
questions_addressed.justification: The connection string in appsettings.json uses SQL Server syntax (Server=localhost;Database=...;User Id=sa;...). The PostgreSQL schema in app/src/db is for reference/testing only.

questions_addressed.question: Should existing in-memory seed data be migrated to SQL database?
questions_addressed.answer: Yes, seed data should be created in SQL database on startup
questions_addressed.justification: Ensures test accounts are available after application restart. Current Program.cs logic will be adapted to use SQL repositories.
questions_addressed.basis: Story analysis requirement: 'Seed data is properly initialized in SQL database'

questions_addressed.question: Should database migrations be automated or manual?
questions_addressed.answer: Automated migrations via Entity Framework Core on application startup
questions_addressed.justification: Simplifies deployment and ensures schema is always in sync with code. EF Core can generate migrations from entity mappings.
questions_addressed.basis: Common pattern in .NET applications for development/testing

questions_addressed.question: What is the complete database schema design for Account and Transaction entities?
questions_addressed.answer: Account: Id (UUID PK), AccountName (VARCHAR 255), CreatedAt (TIMESTAMP), UpdatedAt (TIMESTAMP). Transaction: Id (UUID PK), SourceAccountId (UUID FK), TargetAccountId (UUID FK), Amount (DECIMAL 19,2), TransactionDate (DATE), CreatedAt (TIMESTAMP)
questions_addressed.justification: Domain models in ITransactionRepository.cs and IAccountRepository.cs match the schema design in app/src/db/schema.sql
questions_addressed.basis: Existing domain models and database schema design

questions_addressed.question: Are there any performance or scalability requirements?
questions_addressed.answer: Standard performance for development/testing application; indexes will be created per app/src/db/schema.sql design
questions_addressed.justification: Story analysis indicates standard performance requirements. Database indexes are already designed in schema.sql.

questions_addressed.question: How should the repository pattern be maintained during migration?
questions_addressed.answer: Implement SQL repositories that implement existing ITransactionRepository and IAccountRepository interfaces
questions_addressed.justification: Drop-in replacement approach maintains existing contracts; controllers and services require no changes

questions_addressed.question: How should seed data idempotency be handled?
questions_addressed.answer: Check if accounts exist before creating seed data; use account IDs to prevent duplicates on restart
questions_addressed.justification: Prevents duplicate accounts on application restart. Current Program.cs logic can be adapted to check for existing data.
questions_addressed.basis: Story analysis edge case: 'Seed data already exists in database on application restart'
